final_text:
I looked at the file. The statement is Putnam 2021 B5: if every principal minor of an integer matrix is odd, then so is every principal minor of every power. I can't finish a Lean proof of this within a reasonable effort, so I'm stopping here and have not modified `/work/putnam_2021_b5.lean`.

Reducing mod 2 is the right first step. Over F₂ the hypothesis says every principal minor equals 1. That forces the diagonal to be 1 and b_ij·b_ji = 0 for i ≠ j. The remaining step is showing that B² (and higher powers) keeps all principal minors equal to 1. That needs either a Cauchy–Binet-style expansion of minors of a product or a cycle-cover argument. Neither is available in a form I could verify here, and carrying either through Lean 4 with Mathlib would be a large formalization effort.

I give up.
